title: Oath and Sigil Revisited
premise: In the valley of Hollowmere, where a dead king's dying curse keeps magic from crossing the border, Xanthe Oyelaran has spent his life carving bone charms for the dead and pretending his gift of hearing them is ordinary grief-work. When the crown's witch-hunters breach the valley's ancient wards, Xanthe flees with a ragged found family: Sera, a disgraced huntress; Odji, a child who speaks only in the voices of the dead; and Bramble, a half-starved drake whose dragon-fire is the last living flame of the old kingdom. Together they must find the Door of the Unwritten, the only passage out of a country that officially no longer exists, before Bramble's fire gutters out and takes the last of the old magic with it. Xanthe learns that the dead do not want silence but witness, and in the climax he offers his own name to the Door as the price of passage, trading his erasure from history for his family's survival. The book ends with the family stepping through into a new land, carrying Xanthe's carved bones as their only memory of him, until Odji, now grown, speaks his name aloud and writes him back into the world.
about_author: Rosalind Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former mortuary archivist who spent a decade cataloguing unclaimed remains before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about the unquiet dead and the families we build from strangers, and she still carves small bone tokens for every finished manuscript.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgot Its Name
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. We meet Hollowmere, a valley sealed by a dead king's curse, where Xanthe carves bone charms and quietly hears the dead complain about their unfinished business. When a dying woman's ghost begs him to warn 'the little fire,' he dismisses it as grief-noise. Emotional beat: the loneliness of a man who belongs everywhere among the dead and nowhere among the living.

chapters.title: Hunters at the Wardline
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Crown witch-hunters breach the valley's failing wards, executing a hedge-witch in the market square. Xanthe recognizes the dead king's sigil on their warrant: the hunt is personal, aimed at extinguishing the last royal magic. He realizes the ghost's warning was real. Emotional beat: terror and the shattering of the illusion that hiding was ever safety.

chapters.title: The Child Who Speaks in Borrowed Voices
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Sera, a huntress who deserted after refusing to burn a child, brings Odji to Xanthe's workshop, hunted by her own former captain. Odji speaks only in the voices of the dead, including, briefly, Xanthe's dead mother. Emotional beat: wary strangers forced together, the first fragile stitch of found family.

chapters.title: Bramble and the Guttering Flame
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Following the ghost's warning, they find Bramble, a drake no bigger than a hound, hiding in the bone-carver's cellar, her dragon-fire the last living flame of the old kingdom. Her fire is dying; when it goes out, the Door of the Unwritten will seal forever. Emotional beat: tenderness and dread, responsibility landing on unwilling shoulders.

chapters.title: Roads That No Longer Exist
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. The family flees through a countryside being erased from maps, villages whose names the crown has struck from record. Odji channels a dead cartographer who remembers the road to the Door. Emotional beat: grief for a homeland unmade by decree, and the discovery that memory itself is resistance.

chapters.title: The Captain's Mercy
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Hunted by Sera's former captain Veyra, they are cornered in a burned chapel. Instead of striking, Veyra reveals the crown plans to use captured gifted as fuel to relight its own false dragon-fire, and she is beginning to doubt her orders. Emotional beat: the shock of mercy from an enemy, and the question of whether justice can exist outside the law.

chapters.title: What the Dead Want
chapters.summary: Odji's POV. Through Odji, the valley's dead speak with one voice: they do not want silence, they want witness. They reveal the Door's price, a name freely given, and that the curse on Hollowmere was the dead king's own attempt to protect his people from this hunt. Emotional beat: revelation and the reframing of the dead as allies, not hauntings.

chapters.title: The Door of the Unwritten
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. They reach the Door, a seam of light in a cliff face that exists on no map, guarded by the ghosts of everyone who ever chose exile. Veyra arrives not to arrest them but to buy them time against her own soldiers. Emotional beat: the terrible clarity of the choice ahead, love measured against self-erasure.

chapters.title: A Name Given Freely
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. As the crown's false fire and soldiers close in, and Bramble's flame gutters to an ember, Xanthe gives his name to the Door, trading his place in memory for his family's passage. The Door opens; the dead of the valley hold the hunters back, witnessed at last. Emotional beat: sacrifice as the deepest form of belonging, grief and triumph braided together.

chapters.title: The Bone That Remembers
chapters.summary: Odji's POV, years later. In a new land, the family keeps Xanthe's carved bones as their only relic of him, until grown Odji, who has learned to write as well as speak the dead, carves his name and speaks it aloud, writing him back into the world. Bramble's fire, rekindled, lights the workshop. Emotional beat: resurrection through remembrance, and the promise that no one who is loved is ever truly unwritten.
